_comment: Tunable scoring parameters. Per spec 2.3 there are no hard universal LEVEL thresholds
(no 'claims above 300K = bad'). Levels are scored against each series' own trailing
distribution; momentum is scored against each series' own volatility. The numbers here
govern the STATISTICS, not any indicator's absolute value.
_history_years_note: Trailing window used to build each series' percentile and z-score baseline.
_fetch_years_note: How much history to DOWNLOAD, as opposed to score against. These must differ: the replay needs a full history_years warmup before its first scoreable date, so downloading only ~4 years left barely 11 months of replay - too thin a sample to calibrate on, and it produced a misleading '76% one regime' warning. FRED is free and unlimited, so download generously. 12 years covers 2014 onward, spanning a hiking cycle, a crash, an inflation shock and a cutting cycle.

level_percentile_bands._note: Percentile of the latest value within its trailing window -> level score in [-1, 1], oriented along the pillar axis before polarity is applied.

momentum._note: Momentum compares the short MA to the long MA, expressed in standard deviations of the series' own period-over-period changes. Beyond `strong_sigma` counts as a decisive move.

_anchor_weight_note: How much a STRUCTURAL boundary crossing (curve inversion, Sahm 0.50, NFCI 0) pulls the level score toward its extreme, blended with the percentile score.

pillar_state_bands._note: Weighted pillar score in [-1, 1] -> state name. Bands are symmetric; each pillar's axis direction is defined in fred_series.json.

breadth._note: RSP/SPY ratio drives the breadth read. Thresholds are in percentage points of relative performance over the window.

min_coverage._note: If fewer than this fraction of a pillar's weighted indicators return data, the pillar reports Unknown rather than guessing from a thin sample.

staleness_days._note: Max age before a series is treated as stale. These must account for how FRED DATES observations, not just how often they publish: a monthly series is dated by its REFERENCE MONTH START, so June CPI is dated 2026-06-01 but published mid-July. On 11 August that current print is already 71 days old. Limits set below 100 therefore discard the newest available data as 'stale' in the days before the next release - which collapsed Inflation to 33% coverage on the first live run. Each limit allows the normal reference-to-publication lag plus roughly one missed release.
